intro: Chaliapin returns to the folk-song arrangement with Albert Coates in 1927. The 1928 issue supplies the territorial European public-domain basis for this transfer; US recording status is not established.
question: Where does Chaliapin broaden a phrase in the electrical remake?

cues.title: The arrangement returns
cues.text: Chaliapin sings the same folk-song arrangement with Albert Coates five years after the acoustic side. Compare the shaping of the bass line, remembering that conductor, recording process and transfer have changed as well as the performance date.
cues.evidence: The source identifies Chaliapin, Coates, the arrangers and 20 October 1927: https://pool.publicdomainproject.org/index.php?title=Gramophone-db1103-2-022051. It does not name the orchestra.

cues.title: Carry the repeated line
cues.text: Through the opening, follow the spaces between the sung phrases as well as their sustained notes. Repeated material gives the singer several opportunities to alter emphasis without changing the song’s identity.
cues.evidence: This is a passage-level listening suggestion for the documented folk-song arrangement. The analysis places a measured change near 0:42 but does not identify a particular word, breath or verse.
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: An early crest
cues.text: The recorded level reaches an early crest and then recedes. Compare the length of this rise and withdrawal with 1922, rather than ranking the transfers by apparent volume.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/volga-boatmen-chaliapin-1927.txt: a strong boundary at 0:50 leads towards the high-level 1:00 window; level falls from −9.2 to −17.9 dB by 1:05. Levels are relative within this recording.

cues.title: The middle swell
cues.text: The middle stretch carries another broad increase in recorded level. Listen through its crest to the retreat afterwards, keeping the vocal line distinct from the orchestral support.
cues.evidence: The report lists 1:40 and 1:45 among its loudest windows, with a drop at 1:50. This does not attribute the level change to a separated voice or instrument.

cues.title: A provisional local match
cues.text: Repeated harmony makes this part of the automatic map ambiguous. A sudden change in its timing curve is not proof that Chaliapin abruptly changes speed; use the surrounding phrase as the comparison unit.
cues.evidence: The mapped path around this recording’s 126–145 seconds includes a plateau and compensating jump in the 1922 reference. High cosine similarity does not resolve repeated harmonic material; local tempo claims are withheld.
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: The last sustained span
cues.text: The recorded level stays comparatively high before a longer withdrawal. Follow how the line carries through this last sustained span rather than listening only for the next strong attack.
cues.evidence: The report remains near −10 to −11 dB at 2:20–2:30, then falls to −19.3 dB at 2:40. No exact word or harmonic arrival is timed.

cues.title: Receding into the transfer
cues.text: The closing span lowers the recorded level until the musical sound approaches the disc’s residual noise. Compare the scale of that retreat with the acoustic side, not the absolute amount of hiss in either file.
cues.evidence: The report shows a low-level closing region from 2:40, reaching −31.6 dB at 3:10 and −35.5 at 3:20. Alignment ends at 190 seconds; later noise is not matched.

fields.label: Recorded
fields.note: 1928 is the release year, not the performance date.

fields.label: Matrix, take, sides
fields.note: Commons and the discography identify take 1. The upstream table says “CC-11709-2” but also gives “CC 11709I”; its own cited reference says take 1. The discography lists take 2 as unpublished.

fields.label: Transfer
fields.value: Swiss Foundation Public Domain; Martin Osterwalder collection
fields.note: Collection and institutional transfer provenance are documented; no individual engineer is named.

fields.label: Transfer date
fields.note: The 21 April 2016 Commons upload is not a transfer date.

fields.label: Processing
fields.value: Record cleaning machine and ELP laser turntable
fields.note: The source categories identify Keith Monks Archivist Duo Omni, RCM Mk. IX, and ELP LT-2XA. Detailed restoration, pitch adjustment and equalisation are not documented.

fields.label: Composition rights
fields.value: Traditional melody; Chaliapin–Keneman arrangement is public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms
fields.note: The source gives the arrangers’ deaths as 1938 and 1937. No claim of worldwide clearance is made.

fields.label: Recording rights
fields.value: territorial — European public domain; first published 1928
fields.note: Allowed on documented publication before 1963: the former 50-year recording term expired before the 2013 extension. US recording status is not established. Commons’ PD-old-70 composition tag is not treated as a recording licence; the upstream item contains no non-commercial restriction. Upstream worldwide/US expiry assertions are not adopted.
